title: Shifted local derived comparison with naturality
statement: Let C be a category with Grothendieck topology J, R a sheaf of commutative rings, U an object, and choose a derived category of R|U-modules [def-weil-abstract-derived-category, def-pur-localized-ringed-site]. Let I′ and I be K-injective complexes [def-pur-kinjective-complex], L′ and L arbitrary cochain complexes [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules], s:I′→I and t:L′→L arbitrary chain maps, and n any integer. Degree-n homology of sections of Hom(L,I′) [def-pur-hom-complex] is equivalent to Hom_D(L|U,(I′|U)[n]), and similarly for Hom(L′,I). There exist these two equivalences for which the homology map induced by s and t is sent to derived precomposition by t|U and postcomposition by (s|U)[n]. Neither s nor t is assumed a quasi-isomorphism.

source.place: Equation 21.34.0.1 (0A8Y), Lemma 21.34.6 (0A94), and naturality of componentwise composition

proof.text: Apply the product projections of the Hom complex. Degree-n cocycles satisfy d_I f=(-1)^n f d_L and give chain maps from L|U to (I|U)[n]. Multiplying degree-(n−1) families by (-1)^n identifies coboundaries with null-homotopies. Surjectivity of the homology projection identifies their quotients. This is the shifted form of the localized Hom-complex homotopy comparison.

Restriction preserves K-injectivity and so does shifting. The K-injective localization comparison identifies the homotopy-category Hom sets with the derived-category Hom sets. Use the local comparison in each variable, or Mathlib Qh_map_bijective on the shifted restricted targets.

On cocycle representatives, the bifunctor map is f↦s f t by its product-projection formula. The shift of s has components s^(p+n). These identities prove the naturality equation, which descends to homology since every class has a cycle representative.

lean.statement:
theorem homComplex_sections_derived_naturality
    {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C] {J : GrothendieckTopology C}
    (R : Sheaf J CommRingCat.{max u v}) (U : C)
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (SheafOfModules.{max u v}
      (((sheafCompose J (forget₂ CommRingCat.{max u v} RingCat.{max u v})).obj R).over U))]
    {I' I L' L : CochainComplex
      (SheafOfModules.{max u v}
        ((sheafCompose J (forget₂ CommRingCat.{max u v} RingCat.{max u v})).obj R)) ℤ}
    (s : I' ⟶ I) (t : L' ⟶ L) [I'.IsKInjective] [I.IsKInjective] (n : ℤ) :
    let R₀ := (sheafCompose J (forget₂ CommRingCat.{max u v} RingCat.{max u v})).obj R
    let E := (SheafOfModules.forget R₀ ⋙ PresheafOfModules.evaluation R₀.obj (op U) ⋙
      forget₂ (ModuleCat.{max u v} (R₀.obj.obj (op U))) AddCommGrpCat).mapHomologicalComplex
        (ComplexShape.up ℤ)
    letI := module_overFunctor_preservesZero R₀ U
    let res := (SheafOfModules.overFunctor.{max u v} R₀ U).mapHomologicalComplex
      (ComplexShape.up ℤ)
    let Q := DerivedCategory.Q.{w} (C := SheafOfModules.{max u v} (R₀.over U))
    let f := E.map (((homComplexFunctor (R := R)).map t.op).app I' ≫
      ((homComplexFunctor (R := R)).obj (op L')).map s)
    ∃ a : (E.obj (homComplex (R := R) L I')).homology n ≃
        (Q.obj (res.obj L) ⟶ Q.obj ((res.obj I')⟦n⟧)),
      ∃ b : (E.obj (homComplex (R := R) L' I)).homology n ≃
          (Q.obj (res.obj L') ⟶ Q.obj ((res.obj I)⟦n⟧)),
        ∀ x, b (HomologicalComplex.homologyMap f n x) =
          Q.map (res.map t) ≫ a x ≫ Q.map ((shiftFunctor _ n).map (res.map s))
